independence: All inputs reuse the already sealed original-only reader/boolean corpus. Only the frozen native tool supplies outputs, admissions, transcripts and failed partial files. Capture precedes the Rust byte-string tool migration and all Rust comparisons for this tool corpus; the separate Rust raw reader has already been compared.

seal.cross_profile: Every input and every successful post-operation file agrees byte-for-byte across unchanged Windows and GNU native tools. Platform error codes/stderr and failed partial files are retained independently.
seal.independence: This seal precedes migration of the Rust split/merge implementation to RawGguf. All expected data are native observations; the Rust product and current raw reader supply no expected outputs.

projection: TSV and canonical deduplicated pool mechanically select unchanged original input/after file bytes and success decisions; each source pool slice was SHA-256 checked. Both original profiles retain full raw stdout/stderr, exit codes, partial files and binaries/source identities in their original JSON and byte pools.
scope: All 1605 original reader/boolean inputs passed to split, with max_tensors 1; multi-tensor alias inputs also max_tensors 128. Every successful split with output files is independently merged by the original tool. Admission and successful GGUF bytes agree on Windows/GNU. Source native aborts become checked Rust errors, not reproduced undefined process behavior.
not_claimed: This corpus does not replace the separate 103-case general CLI corpus or the separate source getters/header corpus, and does not close full GGUF/conversion track gates.
